Hypothesis: Warehouse scan latency increased and pushed dispatch/delivery beyond SLA
Test / method: Hub/week comparison; regression with hub and week effects
Evidence (illustrative): Largest estimated contribution: 3.6 pp (45%); p < 0.001 in synthetic demonstration
Measurable target: Reduce 90th percentile scan-to-dispatch time by 30% within 8 weeks

Hypothesis: Route congestion / longer route distance increased transit time
Measures: Route distance, planned vs actual transit, departure time
Measurable target: Reduce late departures on high-risk lanes by 25% in 8 weeks

Hypothesis: Vehicle unavailability and breakdowns reduced on-time performance
Measures: Available fleet %, breakdown and substitute-vehicle events
Measurable target: Raise pre-trip vehicle availability to at least 97%

Hypothesis: Festive-season volume spikes explain most of the decline
Measures: Weekly volume, festive calendar, service mix
Test / method: Seasonal decomposition; event vs non-event comparison
Evidence (illustrative): Seasonality and mix account for about 0.5 pp (6%); non-festive deterioration remains
Measurable target: Publish weekly capacity forecast with forecast error below 10%

Hypothesis: A few hubs or customer segments account for the decline
Measures: Hub, customer tier, service type and region
Test / method: Hub/segment fixed effects; chi-square for late-rate differences
Evidence (illustrative): Concentration is present in affected hubs but hub label changes do not explain the operational effect
Measurable target: Close the gap in the bottom 3 hubs by 2 pp within 10 weeks

Hypothesis: Out-of-order scans and timezone errors created a reporting artefact
Measures: Raw scan timestamps, event sequence, source timezone
Test / method: Reconstruct event chronology; compare raw vs corrected metric
Evidence (illustrative): Corrections alter the measured decline by less than 0.2 pp in the synthetic example
Measurable target: Achieve 99.5% valid event chronology and timezone completeness
